topic.title: Pointers & References
topic.description: Understand memory addresses, pointer arithmetic, and reference semantics.

questions.title: Pointer Arithmetic
questions.explanation: p points to arr[0] (10). p++ makes it point to arr[1] (20). *p is 20. Then arr[1] is incremented by 5 to 25. *(p+1) is arr[2] (30). Finally arr[1] is printed (25).

questions.title: Reference Reassignment
questions.explanation: A reference cannot be rebound. `ref = b;` assigns the value of b (10) to a. When b is later changed to 20, a and ref remain 10.

questions.title: Pointer to Pointer
questions.explanation: The function `modify` takes a pointer-to-pointer. It updates the original pointer `ptr` to point to the static variable `x`. Therefore, `*ptr` prints 100.

questions.title: Array Name Decay
questions.explanation: *arr is arr[0] which is 1. *(arr + 1) is arr[1] which is 2. 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.title: Null Pointer Dereference
questions.explanation: p is a null pointer, so it evaluates to false in the boolean condition. The else block executes, avoiding a crash.

questions.title: Const Pointer vs Pointer to Const
questions.explanation: p is a pointer to a const int. The value pointed to cannot be modified, but the pointer itself can point to a different address.

questions.title: Const Pointer
questions.explanation: p is a const pointer to an int. The pointer cannot point elsewhere, but the value it points to CAN be modified.

questions.title: Function Pointers
questions.explanation: func is a pointer to a function taking two ints and returning an int. It is assigned the address of `add`, so calling it yields 5.

questions.title: References to Pointers
questions.explanation: The function takes a reference to a pointer (`int*&`), allowing it to modify the original pointer `ptr`. It sets it to nullptr.

questions.title: String Literal Addresses
questions.explanation: Most modern C++ compilers perform string pooling, storing identical string literals at the same memory address.

questions.title: Difference between Pointers
questions.explanation: Subtracting two pointers to the same array yields the number of elements between them (4 - 1 = 3).

questions.title: Pointer to Array
questions.explanation: p is a pointer to an array of 3 integers. Dereferencing p yields the array itself, and then [1] accesses the second element.
